atAGlance: Nước ép ổi is guava juice, pale, fragrant, sweet-tart, and sometimes lightly gritty in the way fresh guava should be.
whatItIs: Nước ép ổi is fresh guava juice, sometimes strained, sometimes pulpy. Expect guava juice that is pale, fragrant, lightly gritty, and sweet-tart.
howToEnjoy: Drink it cold and expect a little texture if it is freshly made.
howLocalsOrder: Nước ép ổi is usually made or poured cold, so ask for no sugar, less sugar, or no ice before the glass is finished. Fresh fruit versions taste best when the flavor stays tart, pulpy, or fragrant.
worthKnowing: In Vietnam, Nước ép ổi introduces ổi, a common Vietnamese fruit often eaten with chili salt as well as juiced.
goodToKnow: May be pulpy or lightly grainy.
